title: Fast Times, Slow Times: Timescale Separation in Financial Timeseries Data
hypothesis: Slow variance and tail processes can be separated from fast processes via generalized eigenvalue / nonlinear FastICA criteria and their in-sample relaxation timescales persist out-of-sample.
data_sources: not stated - source/vendor, frequency and price vs return definition not stated; X_t described only as "n-dimensional column vector process (e.g., prices or returns)"
sample:
Three independent baskets, each split into training (in-sample) and continuation (out-of-sample) with weights rescaled to unit gross exposure for plotting. No observation counts, frequency, missing data filters, or Treasury basket composition printed.
- Basket 1 G10 currencies: n=10 implied by "G10" label; tickers/composition not stated; train "2006–2010", test "2010–2025"
- Basket 2 five multifactor equity ETFs: IFSU, IUSZ, IUVL, IUMO, IUQA; n=5; train "2021–2022", test "2022–2025"
- Basket 3 US Treasuries: number of tenors/maturities not stated; train "1994-1998", test "1998-2025"
Overall span implied 1994 to 2025. No sample sizes (N rows) printed.
period_start: not stated as single range - earliest train start printed is "1994-1998" (Treasuries); other baskets start "2006–2010" and "2021–2022"
period_end: not stated as single range - latest test end printed is "2010–2025" (G10), "2022–2025" (ETFs), "1998-2025" (Treasuries); latest calendar year printed is 2025
method: Define X_t as n-dim vector process of prices or returns (exact transform not stated). Define instantaneous variance drift min problem d/dt Var(X_t w_i^T)->min s.t. Var(W X_t^T)=1 ; E[w_i X_t^T X_t w_j^T]=delta_ij.

Variance Timescales (linear, k=1): Solve generalized eigenvalue problem C(t,T) w = lambda C(t,0) w where C(t,0)=covariance, C(t,T)=1/2 E[X_{t+T}^T X_t + X_t^T X_{t+T}] symmetrized autocovariance with lag T, lambda=(1+beta)/2T in [-1,1]. Relation to timescale t_i = -2T/(lambda_i-1). Solve via LAPACK gvd / scipy.linalg.eigh. Extract n eigenvectors; retain 5 slowest (largest lambda_closest to 1 / smallest beta) per basket. Lag T value, data frequency, covariance estimator (sample vs EWMA), demeaning not stated.

Tail Timescales (nonlinear, k=4): Minimize drift of 2k-th moment 1/2k E[(X_t w^T)^{2k}] s.t. E[w_i X_t^T X_t w_j^T]=delta_ij. Solution satisfies (2k-1)E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-2}(dX_t w^T) X_t] + E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1} dX_t]=beta w, beta=2k E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1}(dX_t w^T)]=2k d/dt M_2k, lambda=E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1}(X_{t+T} w^T)] tail autocorrelation order k. Solve numerically via FastICA fixed-point iteration: single component w <- E[X_t d (w^T X_t)^{2k-1}] - (2k-1)E[(w^T X_t)^{2k-2}] w ; w <- w/|w| ; parallel W <- E[X_t d (W^T X_t)^{2k-1}] - (2k-1)E[(W^T X_t)^{2k-2}] W ; W <- (W X_t^T X_t W^T)^{-1/2} W . Convergence tolerance, initialization, max iter not stated.

Empirical fit: For each basket estimate W on training window only: G10 "2006–2010", ETFs "2021–2022", Treasuries "1994-1998". Fit twice: linear tICA k=1 and nonlinear tICA k=4 as defined Sec 2.1/2.2. Increasing k beyond 4 reported as producing no further meaningful changes - threshold not quantified.

Projection: Apply same in-sample W to out-of-sample period without re-estimation: G10 "2010–2025", ETFs "2022–2025", Treasuries "1998-2025". Rescale weights to unit gross exposure for display. Plot resulting portfolios time-series (green background=in-sample, white=out-of-sample) as Figures 1-3: g10/g10k, etf/etfk, tsy/tsyk each with subcaption Linear tICA k=1 vs Nonlinear tICA k=4.

Assessment is visual/qualitative only: compare persistence of weight profiles vs time-series; assess remark: relaxation timescales for slowest components appear remarkably robust out-of-sample with no visible deterioration at in-to-out transition and revert to slow timescale after shocks (e.g. 2008-2010 GFC, 2023 geopolitical events) vs orthogonality of components which decays as expected out-of-sample. No numeric timescale, autocorrelation, deterioration metric, test statistic or p-value printed.
